concerns.question: The three Boolean facts express threshold satisfaction but cannot encode whether that threshold is necessary or sufficient for a licensing obligation. Identical antecedent expressions do not resolve this modal disagreement.

“That business” makes hong_kong refer back to the business described by business. The vocabulary supplies no consistency rule for these related classifications; no independence assumption or truth assignment has been added.

The case-dependent classifications, ordinary-course qualification, and regulatory-intent discussion in Q3 cannot be reconstructed from these three Booleans. They remain external qualifications rather than invented exceptions to the explicit disjunction.
Does “must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation” state a sufficient trigger, or only a necessary threshold whose satisfaction leaves further requirements unresolved?
The three supplied Booleans can express inclusive or cumulative combinations, but cannot supply unspecified additional requirements under the necessary-condition reading.

hong_kong refers to “That business”, so its relationship to business requires consistent external classification. The source does not provide a rule for assigning it when no business exists; unknown inputs must remain unknown.

The ordinary-course qualification, regulatory intent and increased-likelihood language cannot be represented independently by the fixed vocabulary. They remain contextual qualifications, not additional Boolean exemptions.
The supplied facts compress case-dependent legal classifications and resolved carve-outs; they do not establish the content or effect of the missing incorporated authority.
Does “must be present in order to give rise to” identify a sufficient trigger, or only a necessary condition whose satisfaction leaves the licensing obligation unresolved?

Do the business qualifications in Q3 imply a cumulative requirement for regulated activity, business and Hong Kong presence? Such a contextual reading would yield (and regulated business hong_kong), but the supplied text does not expressly require all three and its “at least one” wording weighs against preferring that reading.
What additional requirements, if any, follow from the Circular and Ordinance referenced but not supplied?
